subject: Prefetch fanout latency spike — visibility & status page brief
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood-inference.com>
To: ops@asterhealth.com
Cc: status@statuspage.redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prefetch fanout latency spike — visibility & status page brief

Hi AsterHealth ops team —

We observed a p95 latency spike affecting prefetch fanout for hosted generation requests between 08:50–09:05 PDT. Impact pattern: a small subset of sessions experienced elevated p95 (+600ms) when many short-prefix requests hit prefetch simultaneously. We opened an ops bridge and pushed an interim throttling rule to reduce concurrent fanout to 6 connections per pool (was 12).

What we did so far:
- Activated a mild prefetch throttle at 08:56 PDT (auto-fallback disabled for now).
- Redirected a fraction (~10%) of traffic to an alternate capacity pool to reduce queuing pressure.
- Captured KV and prefix metrics and saved a short diagnostics snapshot.

Customer visible actions:
- Status page entry posted: https://status.redwood-inference.com/incidents/2027-07-prefetch-fanout
- Your calls should see restored p95 within the next 15–30 minutes as the throttle evens out.

Short-term mitigation note: throttle reduces peak concurrency but increases per-request headroom; we expect small request-rate-sensitive customers may see slightly higher initiation latency for a few minutes.

Attachments: prefetch-queue-metrics.png (metric snapshot), prefetch-throttle-config.diff (applied rule)

I'll follow up with a brief customer-impact summary and a proposed postmortem timeline once we stabilize. If you'd prefer a short call, let me know times that work.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

From: AsterHealth Ops <ops@asterhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 09:18:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Prefetch fanout latency spike — visibility & status page brief

Thanks Marcus —

Appreciate the quick heads-up. A couple quick questions: 1) Did any of our scheduled batch jobs (nightly-summaries) coincide with the spike? 2) Do you have a preliminary estimate on how many of our requests were rerouted to the alternate pool?

Also, we need a short blurb we can use internally for our on-call team (one paragraph).

—Rita (AsterHealth)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood-inference.com>
To: ops@asterhealth.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood-inference.com, lauren_bishop@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 10:03:15 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prefetch fanout latency spike — visibility & status page brief

Rita —

Answers inline: 1) We checked job traces; there were two scheduled nightly-summaries running earlier in the window (07:50 PDT) but they do not correlate with the 08:50 spike — this event appears driven by a short burst of low-prefix interactive calls from several customers.

2) Approx 9.8% of your traffic was routed to the alternate pool between 08:56–09:12 PDT. We captured request IDs and included a short CSV in the diagnostics snapshot (see attachment customer-impact-summary.pdf).

Internal blurb (copy for your on-call):
"At 08:50 PDT a prefetch fanout concurrency spike caused p95 to climb for short-prefix generative requests. Redwood applied a targeted throttle and partial reroute; mitigation restored typical p95 within ~12 minutes. If persistent tail latency remains, contact Redwood e2e support."

I'll run a short internal triage and schedule a 30-minute postmortem review at 15:30 PDT today. We'll send a follow-up with a timeline and remediation plan.

—Marcus
